findings.title: WSL lifecycle is not fail-fast
findings.why_it_matters: The release-lifecycle commands are presented as sequential shell input without `set -e` or explicit status chaining. In a normal interactive WSL shell, a failed install, update, or plugin validator does not stop later commands; the final checksum test can still succeed, allowing a prerelease operator or automation wrapper to treat a failed exact-artifact gate as successful.
findings.suggested_fix: Turn the lifecycle block into a checked script beginning with `set -eu` (or join every required command with `&&`), add a cleanup trap, and document that the script's exit status is the gate result.
evidence: docs/testing/wsl2-installer-smoke.md:131-140 invokes install, doctor, update, both plugin validators, uninstall, and checksum verification as independent commands with no fail-fast shell option or status aggregation.
Because the last checksum comparison is independent of the preceding lifecycle commands, it can return zero after an earlier `run_smoke` command returned nonzero.

findings.title: Registration health is only visually confirmed
findings.why_it_matters: `doctor` reports missing or conflicting registrations as prose but does not fail for those states, and the WSL procedure asks the operator to confirm the output manually. A noninteractive prerelease run can therefore pass without proving that both clients registered the supplied artifact-backed server.
findings.suggested_fix: Capture `doctor` output and assert both exact healthy states, for example with `grep -Fx 'Codex MCP registration: owned'` and `grep -Fx 'Claude MCP registration: owned'`, after install and again after update.
evidence: docs/testing/wsl2-installer-smoke.md:132 runs doctor without checking its content, while line 143 delegates confirmation of both registrations to a person.
scripts/install-agent-integrations.sh:1220-1228 prints registration states, and run_doctor completes after reporting them rather than returning nonzero for `missing` or `conflict`.

findings.title: Missing artifact emits raw Node exception
findings.why_it_matters: When MCP_BPMN_PACKAGE_TARBALL names a missing file, the shared package and plugin validation entrypoints expose an uncaught `lstatSync` ENOENT stack trace instead of the input-specific error used for directories and symlinks. Agents must infer whether the path, permissions, or validator failed, adding retries during prerelease automation.
findings.suggested_fix: Catch `lstatSync` failures and emit the same concise MCP_BPMN_PACKAGE_TARBALL correction message used for non-files; add a missing-path test that asserts the stable message and nonzero exit without a stack trace.
evidence: scripts/release-artifact.mjs:20 calls `lstatSync(requestedPath)` outside error handling; only the subsequent type check at lines 21-23 produces the documented environment-input message.
Running `MCP_BPMN_PACKAGE_TARBALL=/definitely/missing/mcp-bpmn.tgz ... node scripts/package-smoke.mjs` exits 1 with a `node:fs` ENOENT stack trace rooted at release-artifact.mjs:20.

residual_risks: The genuine WSL2 procedure could not be executed on this macOS host; command-path and client behavior remain operationally unverified here.
testing_gaps: No automated check proves the documented WSL lifecycle aborts on the first failed install/update/plugin command.
No WSL gate assertion converts Codex and Claude doctor registration states into a machine-checkable failure.
The release-artifact helper lacks a missing-path error-contract test.
